title: A per-session compaction window must not dirty settings.json; the handoff hook must read the window in use
why: shiv, Oct 28 15:20 CDT (via the coordinator): running /autocompact on a session to a value other than 500k writes it into his user settings, which on his machine is the repo's tracked settings.json, leaving a stray line change.
note: Two defects. (1) When shiv runs /autocompact with a value other than 500000, Claude Code writes it into his user settings, which on his machine is the repo's tracked settings.json (autoCompactWindow), so the file shows a stray change. A per-session window must not dirty the tracked file. (2) hooks/precompact_handoff.py read only the top-level autoCompactWindow, so it missed a per-session or per-model value. Partly done: half (2), the hook reading the window in use, shipped in #804 (batch 20, main f7e64677, Oct 29 16:48 CDT). Left: half (1) and the per-tier numbers, which wait on item 61. shiv wants per-tier limits (coordinator 1M on Opus, lanes about 400k, a builder at most 300k) and says local sessions need testing. Measured by the c203 lane, Oct 28 19:45 CDT (cloud, CC 2.1.312): the variable raises the window (1000000 gives effective 980000, 400000 gives 380000); an agent's own autoCompactWindow caps it (the smaller wins, read from the binary's resolver); local launch flags untested. Item 61 offers (a) set the per-tier numbers now, then check the two leftovers (pick), (b) check them first, (c) the generated settings copy; the lane's red test for the settings-copy defect waits on his answer. Port: yes, any repo whose user settings are tracked. Placed after c202 (triage 12, Oct 28). Status set back from done Oct 29 19:06 CDT (coordinator, lane fb-task-homes).
